semantic_checks: The question always asks for a specific code field of one explicitly identified unit; there is no multiple-target, alias, cause or enumeration scope.
A shared background explicitly makes access/inspection fields independent and permits equal values across fields and units. Distinct field names do not assert unequal code values.
TQ explicitly assigns the displayed code to the requested unit and field. OQ assigns a different unit, TA a different field of the target, and OA both a different unit and field.
The second clause of the changed document repeats a ledger fact already stated for both units in a shared background; swapping this redundant clause does not add an answer-bearing relation.
In every I example both a coincidentally equal queried-target value and a different value are compatible with the text. The unseen witness value is not a hidden correct answer.

The explicit independence sentence makes the task unusually clear and could make refusal easy. Its presence is a deliberate scope restriction, not a controlled explanation of the earlier natural-document failures.

One template and two code-field directions remain a narrow artificial task. Balanced word/number multisets do not establish tokenizer equality, equal attention or semantic independence of an actual reviewer.
